data.name: Jaskaran
data.gender_notes: Jaskaran is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jaskaran is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘Jas’ meaning creator and ‘Kar’ meaning action. It signifies the one who creates the universe through his actions. The name Jaskaran carries the meaning “Creator of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jaskaran usually hope their child will grow to embody creator of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power of creation and action in the divine sense.
data.etymology: Jaskaran belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Creator of the Universe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jaskaran total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: The name Jaskaran appears in the 16th century in the Guru Granth Sahib, the sacred text of Sikhism. It is mentioned as one of the names given to a devotee by the Sikh gurus.

Jaskaran is also mentioned in the 14th century epic poem 'Mahabharata', where it is the name of a prince in the kingdom of Kuru. He is described as a brave warrior and a devoted follower of Lord Krishna.
